items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1973-09-07
items.q: Now I like the way Vic Dickerson plays. See now he plays up there you know. He's smooth. He has a nice intonation.

ctx.x: Now I like the way Vic Dickerson plays. See now he plays up there you know. He's smooth. He has a nice intonation. You see what I'm talking about? I love the way Jack Teagarden sang and played, you understand? I met Jack in Texas years ago. I always liked the way he played. I liked the way he sang just like he played. So I've taken a little bit from a lot of fellas. I'm not all that original. But my background and the foundation is New Orleans. I can make those glisters as you'll hear me. You know when I was…
Yeah. But even then your vibrato sounds a little different to me.

items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: And there's Vic. Vic got a style all his own.

ctx.x: Oh you're just talking about the old music, or the old music, or just everybody. Just everybody in the world. Well that's kind of hard because we had a boy that called Big Green. And for playing blues, according to what kind of music played, for playing blues, Big Green, and I love Vic, and it's just, it's kind of hard. The old time. And that was Roy, I'd put Roy against any of them. And that was Jimmy Harrison, I heard him but I never saw him. I didn't hear much of him though. But going from what Lou and them…
I wonder why. Well he never made a lot of records.
